pain_map.pain: The creative opens a price-per-gram evaluation loop it cannot close on-surface: every within-target lifter recognizes the ISO Zero as a legitimate isolate upgrade but the ad presents no per-serving cost, so every engaged buyer defers to an off-ad HealthKart calculation before acting — earned interest leaks between comprehension and consideration, and reorder-cycle inertia (a working concentrate already in the cupboard) frequently absorbs the deferred decision.
pain_map.prevalence: near-universal among within-target enthusiast_macros_lifter across all four contexts

evidence_quotes.quote: I need to see the price per serving before anything else — if isolate pricing pushes it past ₹70-75 a scoop the math stops working and I stay on Performance Whey.

pain_map.pain: The ad fails to articulate a reason-to-switch for buyers already inside the brand's own concentrate line: the isolate's differentiators (2g more protein, lower carb) read as a marginal spec bump against a product that is 'already doing the job', so within-target loyalists who aren't cutting see no job for the upgrade to do — the creative cannibalizes attention without justifying the tier jump, and several resolve to scroll_past outright.
pain_map.prevalence: recurring among within-target lifters, roughly half of whom scroll_past rather than seek info

evidence_quotes.quote: the isolate upgrade has no job to do

I'm not switching from the Performance Whey mid-cycle over an Instagram card.

pain_map.pain: The headline '50% better absorption' claim lands as unverified marketing rather than proof for the most literate buyers: within-target lifters flag it as something they'd need sourced before trusting, and some have already tuned it out from prior exposure — so the ad's central differentiation pitch generates skepticism-to-verify rather than conviction, pushing the decision off-surface instead of closing it.
pain_map.prevalence: several within-target lifters; the absorption claim consistently flagged as unearned

evidence_quotes.quote: The "50% better absorption" claim is the kind of thing I'd want to verify before I trust it.

pain_map.pain: The creative is spending heavily against out-of-target audiences it cannot convert: hair/skin switchers, snackers, and clean-label aspirants uniformly categorize the ad as 'not my world' at the gut beat and scroll past before comprehension — a media-buy targeting/placement inefficiency where the majority of impressions land on dispositions with no category entry point, diluting the within-target signal the brand actually needs.
pain_map.prevalence: overwhelming across all outside-target dispositions and all contexts

evidence_quotes.quote: Whey isolate for muscle protein has no overlap with what I'm actually researching right now — hair and skin supplements.

pain_map.pain: Prior brand experience actively poisons re-engagement for a segment of lapsed users: the same MuscleBlaze identity that grants within-target trust simultaneously triggers 'the tub I binned' recall in lapsed buyers, and the ad offers nothing that addresses why this purchase would end differently — a recall-stage brand-baggage problem that no in-scope creative lever on this SKU resolves for that group (though it is outside-target context).
pain_map.prevalence: consistent across skeptic_lapsed_protein in all contexts

pain_map.prevalence: recurring across skeptic_lapsed_protein and some outside dispositions who clock certifications

commute_scroll.friction_summary: Within-target lifters clock the SKU but explicitly defer price math to a desk session, so the commute context converts interest to 'later' at best.
